steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.

title: TEMPO: Time Series Understanding via Discrete Tokenization
summary: The method replaces ad-hoc signal-to-text serialization or raw feature injection by mapping four-step signal patches to a 625-code discrete vocabulary via a frozen finite-scalar-quantization tokenizer, letting a pretrained LLM process signal tokens, scale statistics, and text jointly with standard self-attention. It costs training a context-aware Transformer tokenizer, extending the embedding matrix, and task-specific fine-tuning with DoRA adapters on a 4B-parameter backbone, which fits within a single 24 GB GPU for inference but adds tokenizer training and fine-tuning complexity. It can fail when the frozen tokenizer's quantization loses signal fidelity on out-of-distribution series, when the 625-code vocabulary under-represents high-frequency dynamics, and when task-specific fine-tuning does not transfer across domains or sensor configurations.
rationale: The approach is reproducible on a single 24 GB GPU with a 4B model and DoRA adapters, but its quantized representation and per-task fine-tuning require validation on the reader's specific time-series workloads before production adoption.
technique: Discrete tokenization of time series for LLMs
